pages.title: Ejecta Rock
pages.text: Stone thrown outward from somewhere nothing should leave. Its grains are shocked and blistered, as if fired out of a white hole, and the strata run backwards: newest at the bottom, oldest on top. It feels lighter than it should.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the ejecta fields I noticed rock whose layers were laid down in reverse order. Only a time-reversed black hole could spit matter out that way. A white hole's leftovers, pushed out the wrong end of time.
